ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points A and B are on the graph of the linear function $y=kx+1$, where point A is in the first quadrant and point B is on the x-axis. Point D is on the positive half of the x-axis, and the coordinates of point C are $(1, -2)$. Quadrilateral OADC is a rhombus. What is the value of $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the coordinates of point C as $\left(1, -2\right)$, and using the properties of a rhombus,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point A are $\left(1, 2\right)$, and of D $\left(2, 0\right)$,\\
substituting point A $\left(1, 2\right)$ into $y=kx+1$ gives $k+1=2$,\\
solving for $k$ yields $k=\boxed{1}$;\\
$\therefore$ the equation of line AB is $y=x+1$.
